title: Dynamic Reservation Windows and Autoscale Guardrails: Quarterly Plan for Dedicated Pools
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: This ticket defines the quarterly roadmap slice for a more adaptive dedicated capacity experience: introduce dynamic reservation windows (DRW), conservative autoscale guardrails, and visibility hooks that tie capacity decisions to unit economics. Goal is to reduce cold failure events and customer-reported throttling during high-variance traffic while limiting committed spend growth and keeping p99 latency SLOs.

Context: Customers on Redwood Dedicated report two recurring issues: (1) sharp traffic spikes lead to transient overloads when autoscale reacts too slowly, causing request failures and degraded latency; (2) long reservation billing cycles and static reserved sizes make it hard to align committed spend with seasonal demand. Existing docs and initiatives (capacity-forecast, reservation-cadence workstreams) provide forecasts and hedging patterns but lack a concrete mechanism to adjust short-term reservation windows automatically and safely.

This initiative proposes three deliverables this quarter: (A) Dynamic Reservation Windows (DRW) - short-duration soft reservations that can be programmatically created by the control plane for 1-72 hour windows to absorb bursts, with explicit cost attribution and opt-in rules; (B) Autoscale Guardrails - conservative ramp/cooldown defaults and a circuit-breaker policy that prefers graceful degradation (queueing / shed non-critical routes) before spinning expensive capacity; (C) Visibility & Billing Hooks - model-level cost telemetry and a reservation-preview dashboard that shows projected unit economics for DRW use.

Goals & Success Metrics (aligned to OKRs):
- OKR: Reduce customer-visible capacity incidents by 50% quarter-over-quarter for targeted customers. Metric: number of dedicated-customer incidents attributed to autoscale failures per month.
- OKR: Keep incremental spend from DRW under 8% of monthly committed spend for participating customers. Metric: ratio of DRW billed dollars to baseline committed monthly invoice.
- OKR: Maintain p99 generation latency within existing SLOs for dedicated pools. Metric: p99 token latency measured per-model for participants.

Scope In: DRW control plane APIs, conservative autoscale defaults + circuit-breaker behavior for Dedicated, dashboard prototype for reservation-preview, billing attribution labels for DRW.
Scope Out: wholesale pricing changes, multi-region DRW federation, VPC-only audit logging (deferred).

Stakeholders: Product: Marco Ibarra (owner), Aisha Kapoor (strategy); Eng: Liam Chen (runtime), Priya Nair (autoscale), Omar Reyes (billing); Design: Evelyn Park (dashboard flow); Sales/CS: Nina Alvarez (customer pilots).

Constraints and trade-offs: DRW increases operational complexity and could temporarily increase committed-like spend; to mitigate we make DRW opt-in and expose a spend cap and TTL. Aggressive autoscale would fix more incidents but increases cost and could cause churn from cost-sensitive customers; we default to conservative ramping and provide knobs to tune per-customer.

Milestones & Timeline:
- Week 1-3: API/contract design for DRW + guardrail config (design review with Eng and Legal for billing labels).
- Week 4-6: Implement minimal control-plane primitives and autoscale policy changes in staging; implement reservation-preview dashboard mockups.
- Week 7-9: End-to-end integration tests, closed pilot with 2 customers, billing tagging verification.
- Week 10-12: Gradual rollout with canary governance and post-deploy incident playbook.

Open Questions:
1) DRW pricing model: flat hourly surcharge vs incremental per-token billing? (Finance leaning to per-token attribution for transparency).
2) Default guardrail parameters: should we prefer queueing with bounded latency or shed low-priority requests first? (Engineering prefers bounded queueing for predictability).

Risks: Billing disputes if DRW not clearly communicated; complexity in autoscale interactions causing oscillations; guardrails reducing availability for critical latency-sensitive routes if misconfigured. Mitigations: explicit opt-in, reservation-preview UI, conservative default values, monitoring and automatic rollback on oscillation patterns.

Related artifacts: see links field for design mockups, PRs, analysis docs.
acceptance_criteria: DRW API v1 spec published and approved by Eng + Legal
Autoscale guardrail rollout implemented in staging with telemetry showing no >5% regression in p99 latency
Reservation-preview dashboard prototype deployed to staging and validated with pilot customers
Billing emits DRW attribution tags for every DRW-reserved allocation and invoice projection matches pilot usage within 3%
Two pilot customers run DRW for at least one burst window with documented lessons and no customer-impacting billing disputes

2025-02-08 | Liam Chen: Reviewed API sketch; flagged risk of oscillation if DRW is created and torn down within cooldown window. Proposed minimal TTL of 30 minutes for DRW allocations.
2025-02-11 | Evelyn Park (Design): Uploaded first-pass reservation-preview wireframes and flow. Recommended emphasizing cost projection in the top fold to avoid surprises.

2025-02-13 | Nina Alvarez (CS): Identified two customers for closed pilot (Acme Health and LexisAI). Acme requires HIPAA impact assessment note; flagged requirement to involve Security for pilot scope. Added a customer pilot checklist.
2025-02-15 | Omar Reyes (Billing): Confirmed billing tags feasibility; suggested final invoices include a DRW line item with start/end times. Will prepare mapping doc to finance schema.

2025-02-18 | Marco Ibarra: Post-planning review with Eng and Finance. Agreed to default DRW billing to per-minute attribution for transparency and to enforce opt-in with spend cap. Decided to keep multi-region DRW out of scope for Q2.
